title: Onam outfit ideas for women
description: Kasavu saree, set mundu and modern Onam looks for women at three budgets, with Kerala brands, prices, jewellery and jasmine hair notes.
intro: Onam dressing is simple on paper: white and gold. In practice you still have choices. Silk or cotton, saree or set mundu, traditional or a modern take. Here are looks at three budgets, plus how to wear a kasavu with confidence.

sections.heading: The white and gold code
sections.body: Kasavu is off-white cotton with a gold zari border. It is the Onam classic. The gold border does the work, so the rest stays quiet. You can change the blouse colour to change the mood. A green, maroon or mustard blouse with a kasavu saree is the usual choice. A set mundu, which is a two-piece version with a blouse and wrap, is easier to wear and walks well.
tips: Kasavu saree with a contrast blouse for the sadhya and the pookalam.
Set mundu if you do not want to drape a saree.
A white kurta set with gold border for the office Onam day.
Choose a border width that suits your height. Narrow borders for petite frames, wider for taller ones.

sections.heading: Outfit formulas
sections.body: Every look has footwear and one accessory.

sections.heading: Colour and silhouette in a white-and-gold look
sections.body: White and gold is the base, so your colour choice goes into the blouse, the border and the jewellery. Warm skin tones suit a rich green or mustard blouse. Cool skin tones suit a maroon, deep blue or wine blouse. A wide gold border pulls the eye along the length of the saree, which suits every height. A narrow border keeps petite frames light. Pleat your saree neatly. Fewer, crisper pleats give a cleaner line than many thick ones. If you wear a set mundu, make sure the waist sits at the natural line and the hem just clears the floor.
tips: Pick a blouse colour that you also own a dupatta for.
Press the pleats the night before.
Match the border colour to your jewellery metal.
Use a thin belt to hold a saree in place on a busy day.

sections.heading: Modern takes
sections.body: If you do not want a saree, wear a kasavu-border dress, a crop top with a long skirt in white, or a white shirt dress with a gold belt. A white linen shirt dress with a thin gold belt looks great and breathes. Keep the colours to white, ivory, cream and gold. Add one bright blouse or dupatta if you want more energy.

sections.heading: Jewellery and hair
sections.body: One-line note: jasmine in a bun or braid, a gold-tone temple necklace and big jhumkas. Parting your hair in the centre and braiding low is a Kerala look that photographs beautifully.

sections.heading: Climate note
sections.body: Onam falls in August or September, in monsoon or just after. Kerala is humid. Wear cotton and handloom. Skip synthetic and heavy silk. Carry a small umbrella, and wear shoes that survive a wet floor.

sections.heading: What to stop buying for Onam
sections.body: Stop buying printed polyester sarees with fake zari. They look shiny in photos and trap heat. Stop buying a new saree every year. Buy a good kasavu once, and change blouses. Stop buying heavy heels for the sadhya. You sit on the floor and walk on wet paths.

faq.q: What do women wear for Onam?
faq.a: Most women wear a kasavu saree or set mundu in off-white with a gold border. Many pair it with a coloured blouse.

faq.q: Can I wear a colour other than white for Onam?
faq.a: Yes. Many wear green, maroon, yellow and mustard. Keep a gold border or accessories to match the festival look.
It is a two-piece kasavu outfit. You wear a wrap skirt and a draped upper cloth. It is easier than a saree.

faq.q: How do I style a kasavu saree?
faq.a: Pair it with a bright blouse, gold jewellery and a low braid with jasmine. Keep makeup light.
